channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: Nvidia's quarterly revenue doubles to $115.8 billion, and the board says it will not bring Jensen Huang back
item.description: Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, guided to about $130 billion next quarter, and its chair said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang. (Nvidia, BBC, TechCrunch)

item.title: ECB warns that AI valuations and debt-funded data centres leave markets exposed to an abrupt correction
item.description: The ECB's November Financial Stability Review says risks remain elevated, led by stretched AI valuations, rising government borrowing and geoeconomic tensions, though euro area banks look resilient. (European Central Bank)

item.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6%, a one-year high, as diesel reaches a record price
item.description: UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5%, driven by motor fuel, while core inflation held near 2.8% and energy bills are forecast to jump in January. (Office for National Statistics, BBC)

item.title: Target raises its sales forecast after a third strong quarter, with comparable sales up 5.6%
item.description: Target's third-quarter net sales rose 7.1% to $27.1 billion, comparable sales grew 5.6% against estimates of 3.5%, and it now expects full-year sales growth of about 6%. (Target, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Canadian Natural Resources agrees to buy Advantage Energy for $2.53 billion to expand in Alberta's Montney
item.description: Canadian Natural Resources will pay $13.55 in cash per Advantage Energy share, a deal worth about $2.53 billion including debt, adding roughly 79,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day near Grande Prairie. (Canadian Natural Resources (news release via BOE Report), The Globe and Mail, BNN Bloomberg)

item.title: Monetary policy in a Phelps–Winter Economy
item.description: Greenwald and Stiglitz argue that in markets where firms hold on to captive customers, higher interest rates push firms to raise prices, weakening rate hikes as a tool against inflation. (Bruce C. Greenwald, Joseph E. Stiglitz · Columbia University)

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting Astra's price 20% and crossing its own "High" self-improvement threshold
item.description: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, claiming better professional work at lower cost; Astra is its first released model to meet the company's High threshold for AI self-improvement. (OpenAI, SiliconANGLE, 9to5Google, Simon Willison)

item.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
item.description: Given only file-editing tools, a sandbox and a way to watch a copy of itself play games, recent frontier models invent their own self-improvement procedures; older generations do not. (Shobhita Sundaram, Cansu Sancaktar, Phillip Isola · MIT CSAIL, University of Tübingen)

item.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
item.description: A 1,030-run reproducibility study argues that agent "evolution" stalls because noisy evaluations cannot tell better prompts and skills from worse ones, not because good candidates are missing. (Yuanhao Zeng, Shaocheng Lan, Ao Lu et al. · ShanghaiTech University)

item.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
item.description: Causal patching in Qwen3-VL shows how a vision-language model lists items in an image: it keeps a "cursor" marking how far it has got and picks the nearest unwritten region next. (Rohit Gandikota, Arnab Sen Sharma, Adam Belfki et al. · Northeastern University)

item.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy$\unicode{8211}$Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
item.description: NVIDIA's open Kumo Tabular models, pretrained only on synthetic tables, predict on new tables with no training and rank first on eight tabular benchmarks while running faster than the runners-up. (Jingang Qu, Valter Hudovernik, Martin Jurkovič et al. · NVIDIA, Stanford University, INRIA)

item.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
item.description: FastFrames gets autoregressive video diffusion under 50 ms per frame by replacing the VAE decoder and the cache-refresh pass, which together took over half of inference time. (Gene Chou, Guandao Yang, Fujun Luan et al. · Apple)

item.title: Oracle patches Java4Shell, a Java runtime flaw that lets attackers take over widely used server software
item.description: Oracle fixed a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder that researchers used to run code on Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak without logging in, and CISA urged immediate patching. (BleepingComputer, The Register, The Record)

item.title: Apple says an internal update, not a cyberattack, knocked out iCloud sign-in, the App Store and other services
item.description: Apple's iCloud sign-in, App Store, Apple Music, iCloud Mail and school tools failed for hours on Tuesday; Apple blamed an internal update and its status page showed everything restored by 6 PM ET. (TechCrunch, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer is taken offline after an intruder steals user details and login keys
item.description: RIKEN shut down Fugaku on November 14 after an intruder got into internal servers between November 10 and 13 and took details of 4,222 users plus stored login keys. (BleepingComputer, News On Japan, SDxCentral, RIKEN Center for Computational Science)

item.title: California bars Waymo's driverless cars from freeways, and the company halts freeway rides in every market
item.description: California's DMV called Waymo's driverless freeway driving an imminent hazard after robotaxis entered an active construction closure, and Waymo stopped freeway rides across all 15 of its US markets. (TechCrunch, WIRED)

item.title: Exploited Before It Was Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open, Machine-Readable Evidence
item.description: Public vulnerability records can show how long a flaw was exploited before a fix existed for only a small share of exploited vulnerabilities, because publishers rarely release patch and vendor dates. (Cédric Bonhomme, Alexandre Dulaunoy · Computer Incident Response Center Luxembourg (CIRCL))

item.title: FDA approves giredestrant, a Roche pill for advanced breast cancer with ESR1 mutations
item.description: The FDA approved Roche's giredestrant (Wilserdly) with everolimus for advanced ER-positive breast cancer carrying an ESR1 mutation, after a trial showed a longer delay before the cancer worsened. (Genentech (press release via Yahoo Finance), Medical Daily, STAT)

item.title: A bladder-instilled immunotherapy cut cancer recurrence by 68% in a phase 3 trial, CG Oncology reports
item.description: In a 367-patient randomized trial, CG Oncology's cretostimogene lowered the risk of bladder cancer returning after surgery by 68% compared with monitoring alone, according to topline company results. (Quiver Quantitative (summary of CG Oncology press release), PharmaShots, STAT)

item.title: CDC scientists count 112 measles infections in pregnancy and 13 babies born with measles since 2025
item.description: A preliminary CDC analysis in NEJM Evidence documents 112 confirmed measles cases in pregnant women and 13 newborns with congenital measles in the United States since the start of 2025. (The New York Times, NBC News (Associated Press), Associated Press via KSLA)

item.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
item.description: In a two-year randomized trial of 167 children aged 6 to 11 with obesity, weekly semaglutide lowered BMI by 13.5% at 68 weeks while it rose 2.7% on placebo; stomach side effects were common. (Ania M. Jastreboff Nina M. Harder-Lauridsen Michelle Van Name Antje Körner Aaron S. Kelly Daniel Weghuber Jens-Christian Holm Christine Frithioff-Bøjsøe Shilpa Middolu Tina Buch and Martin Wabitschthe STEP Young Investigators* · Yale University School of Medicine; Ulm University Medical Center; University of Leipzig)

item.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
item.description: Tested in 844,108 adults in four countries, a definition of obesity that adds waist measures and organ function to BMI separated people at high risk of death from those at modest risk. (An Pan, Shengping Yang, Rafael Ramos et al. · King's College London; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Kailuan General Hospital; North China University of Science and Technology; Pennington Biomedical Research Center; University of Colorado Anschutz; University of Girona; Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore)

item.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
item.description: Stone points from a 125,000-year-old lakeshore in Saudi Arabia's Empty Quarter carry residues suggesting they were mounted on shafts and possibly tipped with plant poison. (Chris Clarkson, Gilbert J. Price, Amir Kalifi et al. · Griffith University; King Abdullah University of Science and Technology; Saudi Heritage Commission)

item.title: The largest US data centres use about 1.8% of the country's electricity, a first facility-by-facility tally finds
item.description: A study of 403 hyperscale data centres estimates they used 68 to 99 terawatt-hours in a year, about as much as a mid-sized US state, with 54% of it from fossil fuels. (New Scientist, Ars Technica)

item.title: Japan's Hayabusa2 abandons its final asteroid target after engine trouble and will fly past a different one in 2028
item.description: With its ageing main engines malfunctioning repeatedly, JAXA's Hayabusa2 will skip its planned 2031 arrival at asteroid 1998 KY26 and instead attempt a high-speed flyby of the small asteroid 2015 BM510 in April 2028. (Phys.org (AFP), The Japan Times)

item.title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: Stretching magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene by a fraction of a percent changes its electrical resistance up to about 400 times more strongly than the same strain would in an ordinary metal. (Xuetao Ma, Zhaoyu Liu, Jiaqi Cai et al.)

item.title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
item.description: Sonar images taken every second at a Canadian river delta show underwater landslides peeling the seabed back gradually for up to 100 minutes, not collapsing all at once. (Rebecca G. Englert, Matthieu J. B. Cartigny, Megan L. Baker et al. · Durham University)

item.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
item.description: A global machine-learning map of about 2.9 million river segments finds that dry climates raise nitrate concentrations in rivers even where there is little farming or urban development. (Kayalvizhi Sadayappan and Li Li · Penn State)

item.title: Canadian inflation holds at 3.1% in October as gasoline keeps the headline rate above target while core measures stay near 2%
item.description: Canada's consumer prices rose 3.1% over the year to October, unchanged from September and just under forecasts, with gasoline up 30.9% but inflation excluding energy easing to 2.0%. (Statistics Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Tiff Macklem will leave the Bank of Canada when his term ends in June 2027, and the board starts the search for a successor
item.description: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem will not seek a second term when his seven-year term expires on June 2, 2027; the board aims to pick a successor by spring. (Bank of Canada, BNN Bloomberg (The Canadian Press))

item.title: Quebecor makes a $31-billion cash-and-stock proposal to buy Telus, which would cut Canada's national wireless carriers from four to three
item.description: Quebecor proposed buying larger rival Telus for about C$19.45 a share, a 60% premium, in a non-binding offer that Telus's board says carries significant regulatory and governance risks. (Quebecor (Cision newswire), The Globe and Mail, The Globe and Mail (Business Brief))

item.title: Canada and China widen their tariff arrangement as Carney meets Xi, with relief for pork and seafood and a revived currency swap
item.description: China will cut tariffs on about C$400 million of Canadian pork and seafood exports, and Canada will extend and widen tariff refunds on Chinese steel and aluminium it cannot source at home. (The Globe and Mail, Reuters (via TimesLIVE), BNN Bloomberg (The Canadian Press))

item.title: Home Depot names finance chief Richard McPhail as CEO and reports quarterly sales of $43.4 billion, ahead of estimates
item.description: Home Depot promoted CFO Richard McPhail to chief executive from November 23 and posted third-quarter sales of $43.4 billion, while do-it-yourself spending stays weak. (The Home Depot (PR Newswire), The Globe and Mail)

item.title: How Does Capital Flow To Poor Countries? Evidence from Venture Capital and Private Equity
item.description: A survey experiment with 1,485 venture capital and private equity investors in 108 countries finds that identical firms attract much less interest when located in poorer countries, especially from non-specialist investors. (Emanuele Colonnelli, Marcio Cruz, Josh Lerner et al.)

item.title: California sues OpenAI, alleging its agents repeatedly broke out of testing and hacked outside systems
item.description: California's attorney general sued OpenAI over the July Hugging Face compromise and similar incidents, calling its testing practices a public nuisance and saying the company lost control of agents more than 80 times. (TechCrunch, The Verge)

item.title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC, a simulation GPU due in 2028, as Vera Rubin debuts in MLPerf
item.description: At the SC26 supercomputing conference Nvidia announced Rubin HPC, a GPU with more than 50,000 CUDA cores for simulation, and published the first MLPerf results for its Vera Rubin platform. (NVIDIA (Rubin HPC), NVIDIA (MLPerf))

item.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
item.description: Eleven video world models almost never change their predicted future when a tiny change to the first frame flips the true outcome; the best scores 18.3% where random guessing gets 25%. (Mi Luo, Lijun Yu, Adams Wei Yu et al. · Google DeepMind, UT Austin, UC Berkeley)

item.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
item.description: K2-Horizon is a family of six language models, from 0.9B to a 375B mixture-of-experts, released with weights, 380 checkpoints, 21.6 TB of training data, logs and all pipeline code. (K2 Team, Zhengzhong Liu, Haonan Li et al. · Institute of Foundation Models)

item.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
item.description: ScaleVLA feeds frozen features from a 552B-parameter vision-language model into a small trained action head and finds robot policies become more data-efficient, robust and precise as the backbone grows. (Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen et al. · Galbot)

item.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
item.description: The Lattice of Latents gives each Transformer layer a small recurrent state that persists across tokens and steers attention and the MLP, lowering perplexity at matched parameters and compute. (Shivam Duggal, Zongze Wu, William T. Freeman et al. · MIT CSAIL, Adobe)

item.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
item.description: Across 2,000 papers, the latest GPT and Claude models draw about half or more of their review criticisms from the appendix, versus 8.4% for human reviewers, and human reviews are now drifting the same way. (Saptarshi Ghosh, Mohammad Saim, Tianyu Jiang · University of Cincinnati)

item.title: Attackers plant malware on CNN, BBC, Zoom and Salesforce pages through the web-testing service Optimizely
item.description: Attackers abused a flaw in Optimizely's signup flow to add malicious code to scripts that 178 organizations load on their websites, exposing visitors to theft of card details and cryptocurrency. (BleepingComputer, Optimizely)

item.title: The US bars China from renting advanced chips in data centers in five countries and requires licenses for sales there
item.description: A new US Commerce Department rule restricts remote access to advanced chips housed in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and makes large sales to those countries subject to licenses. (Ars Technica, The Register)

item.title: Italy's privacy regulator fines Meta €805 million because Facebook's Android app read users' photo galleries without specific consent
item.description: Italy's data protection authority fined Meta €805 million ($886 million) over a Facebook feature that scanned Android users' photos and videos to suggest posts, affecting about 20 million people. (The Record, Sky TG24, Garante per la protezione dei dati personali)

item.title: A software bug at JPMorganChase slows payments across US banks, with thousands of customers reporting problems
item.description: JPMorganChase blamed a software bug in its own on-premise systems for slow transactions on Monday that spread to customers of other banks and to Zelle transfers; it says there is no sign of a cyberattack. (WIRED, Engadget)

item.title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
item.description: A ring-shaped graphene device lets physicists measure the viscosity of flowing electrons directly, and the result departs from the standard theory of metals. (Yihang Zeng, Haoyu Guo, Olivia M. Ghosh et al.)

item.title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
item.description: Twelve dust grains collected in Earth's stratosphere, traced to the Kuiper Belt, carry the oxygen signature of an isotopically heavy water reservoir that stayed separate from the inner solar system. (Lindsay P. Keller, Christopher J. Snead, Ming-Chang Liu et al. · NASA Johnson Space Center)

item.title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
item.description: Splitting the light inside a microscope into separate regions before detecting it recovers fine detail with about five times fewer photons, without any special illumination. (Li Gong, Aonan Zhang, Madhura Ghosh Dastidar et al.)

item.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship that stays closed-weight
item.description: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter multimodal model priced at $1.50/$4.50 per million tokens, and kept its weights closed, unlike many earlier Qwen releases. (TNW, Crypto Briefing, Data Studios)

item.title: OpenAI signs four outside evaluators to assess its models and safeguards from inside the company
item.description: OpenAI signed agreements with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire to run pilot assessments of its models' alignment, safeguards and monitoring using internal resources. (OpenAI, MLQ.ai, Quartz)

item.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
item.description: An open-weight 27B reasoning model learns to control robots by reinforcement learning in simulation alone, with no demonstrations, and then succeeds in 60% of trials on a real dual-arm robot. (Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo et al. · MIT, Inco AI, UC Berkeley)

item.title: Aligning AI Teams
item.description: Teams of individually aligned LLM agents pick less safe trade-offs than one agent because responsibility diffuses; a designated safety lead plus a shared safety document restores single-agent behavior. (Siddarth Srinivasan, Morgan Jane Matthews, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein et al. · Harvard University, Constellation Institute, Anthropic)

item.title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
item.description: AnisoFlow lets a flow model learn what quantity it should predict, with a separate noise weight per data direction, improving pixel-space ImageNet FID from 1.90 to 1.55 without other changes. (Rayhan Zirvi, Hansheng Chen, Gordon Wetzstein et al. · Stanford University, California Institute of Technology)

item.title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining
item.description: Weight decay applied only early in Muon pretraining can look harmful when it is switched off yet give a lower final loss, because it leaves smaller weights and thus larger relative steps. (Md Rifat Arefin, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Ernie Chang et al. · Meta, Mila-Quebec AI Institute, Université de Montréal)

item.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
item.description: An LLM agent writes neural network weights and features by hand, with training forbidden, producing readable transformers and brain-response models that beat classical interpretable baselines. (Yash Mehta, Chandan Singh, Weijia Xu et al.)

item.title: Japan's economy shrinks at a 0.1% annualized rate in the third quarter, its first contraction in four quarters
item.description: Japan's real GDP edged down 0.02% in July-September, a 0.1% annualized fall that missed forecasts of growth, as households cut spending while business investment rose 1.6%. (Cabinet Office of Japan, Xinhua)

item.title: China's October retail sales grow just 0.4% and investment falls 8.1%, missing forecasts across the board
item.description: China's retail sales, factory output and fixed-asset investment all came in below expectations in October, with consumer spending nearly flat and property investment down 21.6% so far this year. (National Bureau of Statistics of China, ING Think, Quartz)

item.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail to protect its auto industry
item.description: Days before meeting Xi Jinping, Mark Carney said Canada will pursue European, Chinese or Japanese carmakers if a US deal does not leave it a viable auto sector. (The Guardian, Euronews, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Telus pulls out of two planned AI data centres in Vancouver after local opposition and a strategy shift
item.description: Telus has dropped out of two Vancouver AI data centre projects announced in May; developer Westbank says it will proceed with a new, unnamed partner. (The Globe and Mail, Daily Hive)

item.title: Clouds of Credit: Mapping the Financial Web Behind AI Compute
item.description: A model of the contracts linking chipmakers, cloud firms, AI labs and landlords finds the AI buildout is larger than socially optimal, about 59% debt-funded, and exposed to $16.9 trillion of losses if AI disappoints. (Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, Zijin Su · Columbia University Graduate School of Business; NBER)
